v1.7.0 closes out the 1.6 series — 182 pull requests across thirty patch releases since v1.6.0 — the series that took the platform from the LadybugDB 0.18 foundation to a launch-ready product: a full forecasting engine, multi-user organizations, hardened billing and storage accounting, and, capping the series in this release, direct remote MCP connectivity for every graph.

## Remote MCP connectivity

- **Remote MCP transport** — every graph now serves the MCP Streamable HTTP transport at `POST /v1/graphs/{graph_id}/mcp`: full JSON-RPC lifecycle, server-chosen SSE-on-POST streaming with progress notifications, and queued queries bridged onto the SSE stream. Paste a graph URL into Claude, Claude Code, or Cursor and go — same tools and same authorization path as the npx bridge, no local process required. Subgraphs are addressed as their own connector URLs via `switch-workspace`.
- **`sync-connection` MCP tool** — agents can trigger a connection resync themselves (for example, clearing a stale-sync blocker during a month-end close). The REST sync endpoint and the tool run on one shared kernel, so both surfaces validate, lock, and dispatch identically.
- **Per-graph instructions and legibility** — MCP handshakes now carry graph-aware instructions, and the forecasting and schedule surfaces gained descriptions and envelopes written for operator comprehension.

## Forecasting and the operating plan

- **Operating-plan scenarios** — driver-based forecasting over the ledger with four scenario types (including per-line growth), producing full articulated statements
- **Statement series and close stamps** — monthly statement series anchored to period-close stamps, with plan backfill to seed history
- **Line assertions and articulation** — per-line assertions with rollup checks; the cash-flow statement ties to the balance-sheet cash delta
- **Series windowing and envelope correctness** — windowed series reads with a batch of surface-correctness fixes landed across the series

## Information-block and disclosure authoring

- **Non-numeric fact substrate** — text and other non-numeric facts as first-class information-block content, with text-block binding into disclosures
- **Disclosure rendering and authoring** — a render substrate for authored disclosures, exercised end-to-end by the authoring demo
- **Metric definitions and chart views** — a metric-definition grammar, assertable metric series, chart-view projections, and an event-source registry for ingesting custom metric events

## Multi-user organizations

- **Invitations and roles** — organization invitations with invited-registration flow, role checks on graph access, and graph creation restricted to org admins
- **Org-scoped billing** — repository subscriptions at the organization level, aligned billing visibility, and usage rollups scoped to the org

## Billing and subscription correctness

- **Credit integrity** — a single authoritative credit-balance definition, usage-ledger credit events, webhook retry with credit refill, and correct webhook subscription resolution
- **Pricing operations** — upcoming-invoice preview, graph tier resize with repricing, repository-subscription lifecycle hardening, and tier-differentiated rate limits

## Data plane and storage

- **Volume lifecycle** — atomic volume claims, instance-registry reconciliation and replica discovery, and stale-claim cleanup
- **Storage accounting** — measured instance footprints reported on the dashboard, in admin tooling, and enforced consistently on the ingestion and materialization paths (refuse rather than skip when usage cannot be verified)
- **Materialization safety** — partial materializations no longer swap in, staged rematerialization is guarded, and SEC materialization gained incremental loading plus Arrow batch-size and memory fixes
- **Replica reliability** — admission headroom guards, warmup-aware alarms, boot-timeout and load-balancer fixes on the shared-replica fleet, and zstd-compressed backups

## Taxonomy and reporting

- **Extension authoring hardened** — library namespace protection, environment-gated authoring, and cascade-integrity fixes for tenant taxonomy extensions
- **Calc-DAG guardrails** — rollup validators and regeneration guards protecting statement calculation structure
- **Fact grid** — entity dimensions and result limits on the fact-grid surface, plus duration-collapse correctness

## Security and compliance

- Authorization hardening across the operator and extensions write surfaces, and query-surface input-validation improvements
- Third-party penetration test findings remediated and verified in production
- Shared-repository query telemetry with per-user attribution and expanded CloudWatch alarm coverage
- Infrastructure posture work supporting the SOC 2 program: credential rotation, extended log retention, TLS and encryption hardening, and continuous-monitoring coverage

## Platform and developer experience

- **Client SDKs at 1.0** — the Python and TypeScript SDKs graduated to semver 1.0 contracts, with typed reads adopted throughout the examples
- **Document usage reporting** — `GET /v1/graphs/{graph_id}/limits` now includes a `documents` section against the tier cap
- **Developer environment** — Windows/WSL2 support, a Docker upgrade command, and dependency currency across Dagster, OpenTelemetry, and LanceDB
- **Release process** — curated release notes for milestones now live in `.github/release-notes/` (this release is the first to use the convention)

## Upgrading from v1.6.0

- Nine database migrations landed across the series (four platform, five extensions) — run both migration histories
- The usage surface was renamed from `analytics` and operation IDs were normalized mid-series, before the SDK 1.0 contract took effect; regenerate any pre-1.0 clients
- CloudFormation updates ride the deploy across the series, including new alarms and a metric filter on the shared-replicas stack in this release
- v1.7.0 itself contains no breaking API changes; the remote MCP endpoint is additive and excluded from the OpenAPI schema
